gloss: to irritate; to annoy; to frustrate

definitions.gloss: to irritate; to annoy; to frustrate
definitions.explanation: To cause someone to feel irritated, annoyed, or frustrated. The causative form of {苛立|いらだ}つ.

examples.japanese: その{態度|たいど}が{私|わたし}を{苛立|いらだ}たせる。
{彼|かれ}の{遅刻|ちこく}がみんなを{苛立|いらだ}たせた。
{何度|なんど}も{同|おな}じミスを{繰|く}り{返|かえ}す{部下|ぶか}に{苛立|いらだ}たせられた。
examples.english: I was frustrated by the subordinate who kept repeating the same mistakes.

notes:
The causative form of {苛立|いらだ}つ (to be irritated). While {苛立|いらだ}つ describes the state of being irritated, {苛立|いらだ}たせる focuses on the cause — what or who is producing the irritation. Often used with the passive {苛立|いらだ}たせられる (to be made to feel irritated by).

COMMON PATTERNS:
- ～が{人|ひと}を{苛立|いらだ}たせる: something irritates someone
- ～に{苛立|いらだ}たせられる: to be irritated by something
- {苛立|いらだ}たせるような: irritating, annoying (modifying a noun)

RELATED WORDS:
- {苛立|いらだ}つ: to be irritated, to feel frustrated (the base intransitive verb)
- {苛立|いらだ}ち: irritation, frustration (noun form)
- イライラさせる: to irritate (more colloquial, onomatopoeic)
- {怒|おこ}らせる: to anger, to make angry — stronger emotion than irritation
